prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an outdoor street-corner scene where the ground plane slopes continuously downward and away from the camera wearer's elevated head viewpoint, while distant buildings and across-the-street pedestrians fade into black beyond roughly 5–10 metres. In frames 1–3, the person in the maroon jacket stands in the immediate left-foreground at roughly 0.3–0.6 metres (within arm's reach) alongside the camera wearer's own extended right forearm and hand at ~0.4 metres at the bottom right, occluding the woman in the black jacket and blue backpack (~1–1.5 metres away in frame 1) and the woman in the olive jacket (~1.5–2 metres away to the left in frame 2). Across frames 3–5, the woman in the black jacket and the woman in the olive jacket step forward onto the green corner curb to roughly 2–2.5 metres in front of the camera wearer (~0.5–1 metre apart from each other), while the maroon-jacketed person drops mostly out of view at the bottom-left edge (<0.5 metres) as the camera pitches downward. A passing red car in frames 2–3 (~4–8 metres away) and a left-moving motorcyclist in frame 4 (~3.5–4.5 metres away) appear as mid-grey silhouettes behind the pedestrians. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the overlapping foreground layers in frames 1–3 by brightness, though it becomes unreliable beyond ~6 metres where the street surface, buildings, and distant vehicles merge into uniform darkness.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and background actors across the street intersection, separating the close maroon-jacketed person (~0.3–0.6 metres left, facing right/forward away from the wearer) and the camera wearer's own lower-right arm (<0.5 metres, within arm's reach) from the two companions in the black and olive jackets (~1–2.5 metres ahead and ~0.5–1 metre apart). As the sequence progresses from frame 1 to frame 5, the masks show the woman in the black jacket passing from behind the maroon-jacketed person's left side (frame 1) around their front (frame 3) to stand at the curb edge facing away toward the street (frames 4–5, raising her right arm in frame 5), while the woman in the olive jacket advances on her left with a backpack/handbag within her own reach. It also captures the red car driving away from ~4 to ~8 metres in frames 2–3, a motorcyclist passing right-to-left at ~3.5–4.5 metres in frame 4, and small clusters of pedestrians across the street at ~8–15 metres. This map makes distant pedestrians on the far sidewalk and overlapping bags (such as the blue backpack in frame 4 and black backpack in frame 5) easier to spot than in a quick glance at RGB. However, it is unreliable in several places: it mislabels the camera wearer's own arm as a separate 'person' in frames 1–2 (and misses it in frame 4), hallucinates a 'tennis racket' on a street marking in frame 1, fragments the motorcyclist and rider into 'backpack' and 'person' masks in frame 4, and misclassifies part of the olive-jacketed woman's legs/bag as 'motorcycle' and 'handbag' in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across all five frames, detecting only a single yellow body skeleton in frame 2 for the woman in the olive jacket standing roughly 1.5–2 metres to the left of the camera wearer. That skeleton shows her in profile facing right (toward the maroon-jacketed person's back and the street intersection, not looking at the camera wearer), with her head above her upright torso, her left arm bent at the elbow with her hand near her hip/pocket within her own reach, and her legs split in a stepping stance near the curb. Because every other frame is completely black, the map provides no information on how people move, approach, or turn across the 5-frame sequence, nor does it show the camera wearer's own visible hand within arm's reach. While frame 2's skeleton clarifies the exact joint positions of the olive-jacketed woman's bent arm and stepping legs through her dark clothing and backpack occlusion better than RGB alone, the pose map is highly unreliable overall. It completely misses the maroon-jacketed person (~0.3–0.6 metres away, heavily truncated by the frame edges), the woman in the black jacket (~1–2.5 metres away), the motorcyclist (~4 metres away), all distant pedestrians, and all magenta hand skeletons across the entire strip.
